In my opinion, working from home have more advantages than disadvantages. People can save the time they spend in the traffic, and they can organize better their day. However, some persons feel alone and it is difficult to separate the work and the personal life.

segments.text: In my opinion, working from home

segments.why: The subject 'working from home' is singular, so use 'has'.

segments.text: more advantages than disadvantages. People can save the time they spend

segments.why: Use 'in traffic' without the article.
Adverbs like 'better' usually come after the object, not between the verb and object.
'People' is the natural plural; 'persons' sounds formal or legal.
'Lonely' describes the feeling of isolation; 'alone' just means without others.

segments.text: and it is difficult to separate work and

segments.why: Don't use 'the' with general uncountable ideas like work and personal life.

out.tip: Remember that general ideas like traffic, work and personal life usually don't need 'the' in English.

what: Drill from your real saved mistakes
input:
Learner level: B1
Explanation language: English

Frequent mistakes:
- word choice / collocation: pick a side (1x), e.g. "take" → "pick"
- time expression word order (1x), e.g. "a few decades ago was impossible" → "was impossible a few decades ago"
- contrast structure and word choice (determine vs decide) (1x), e.g. ", but how people use it decides that" → "; rather, how people use it determines that"
- collocation: take sides (1x), e.g. "a side" → "sides"

items.wrong: In the meeting, my manager refused to take a side in the argument between the two teams.
items.right: In the meeting, my manager refused to take sides in the argument between the two teams.
items.hint: This fixed expression uses a plural noun when you support one person or group against another.

items.wrong: Working from home was almost impossible a few decades ago, but now many companies offer it.
items.right: Working from home was almost impossible a few decades ago, but now many companies offer it.

items.wrong: A few years ago was difficult to book flights online from small airports.
items.right: It was difficult to book flights online from small airports a few years ago.
items.hint: Put the time expression at the end of the clause and make sure the sentence has a subject.

items.wrong: Travel apps are not good or bad in themselves, but how tourists use them decides that.
items.right: Travel apps are not good or bad in themselves; rather, how tourists use them determines that.
items.pattern: contrast structure and determine vs decide
items.hint: Use a contrast linker like 'rather', and choose the verb meaning 'to be the factor that causes a result'.

items.wrong: When my friends argue about politics, I never take a side; I just listen.
items.right: When my friends argue about politics, I never take sides; I just listen.
items.hint: Think about whether this expression is singular or plural.

items.wrong: Both candidates were good, so it was hard to take one for the job.
items.right: Both candidates were good, so it was hard to pick one for the job.
items.pattern: word choice / collocation: pick vs take
items.hint: Which verb means 'choose' from several options?

items.wrong: The price of the hotel is not the only factor, but the location decides how much we enjoy the trip.
items.right: The price of the hotel is not the only factor; rather, the location determines how much we enjoy the trip.
items.pattern: contrast structure and determine vs decide
items.hint: Use a stronger contrast structure, and pick the verb for a factor that influences an outcome.

items.wrong: Our company opened a second office in Madrid a few years ago, but was closed last year.
items.right: Our company opened a second office in Madrid a few years ago, but it was closed last year.
items.hint: Check the second clause: it needs a subject, and the time expression stays at the end.

Mistake type: present perfect vs past
Expected fix: I finished the report yesterday.

out.note: The learner's version 'I completed the report yesterday' is a mix of past perfect and present perfect tenses. A correct sentence would be 'I finished the report yesterday.' The past perfect tense describes a completed action in the past, while the present perfect tense describes an action that started in the past and continues in the present. The mistake is not present, but rather the incorrect use of the auxiliary verb 'completed' instead of 'finished'. A correct sentence would use 'finished' instead.
